topic: Connecticut Uniform Trust Code (CUTS) applicability and nonuniform provisions
rule_summary: Connecticut has enacted the CUTS with significant nonuniform provisions from the model UTC. CUTS applies to express trusts formed or administered in Connecticut. Specific departures from model UTC require case-by-case review.
exceptions: Statutory trusts formed under specific Connecticut enabling statutes.
Nonuniform provisions govern creditor rights, spendthrift enforceability, and self-settled trust rules.
open_questions: How courts interpret specific nonuniform CUTS provisions in light of other states' UTC precedent.

rule_summary: Trust creation requires written instrument for land trusts, lawful purpose, ascertainable beneficiaries or charitable purpose, trustee acceptance, and settlor capacity. Oral trusts for personal property recognized subject to proof.
exceptions: Oral trusts for personal property require clear and convincing evidence.
Charitable purpose trusts exempt from beneficiary ascertainability.

topic: Connecticut self-settled trust — no asset protection
rule_summary: Connecticut explicitly prohibits spendthrift protection for self-settled trusts. A settlor who creates an irrevocable trust for their own benefit cannot claim creditor protection under Connecticut law. Third-party settled trusts ARE protected.
exceptions: Third-party settled trusts retain spendthrift protection.
open_questions: Whether specific trust structures or spendthrift clause language affect the self-settled rule.

topic: Connecticut spendthrift enforcement for third-party settled trusts
rule_summary: Connecticut enforces spendthrift clauses in third-party settled trusts. Exception creditors (support, government, tort) may reach protected distributions.
Connecticut CUTS authorizes directed trustees, investment advisers, and distribution advisers with fiduciary obligations when following directions.
exceptions: Improper directions create directed trustee liability.

rule_summary: Connecticut decanting statute authorizes trustees with discretionary power to distribute to a second trust. Beneficiary notice and court approval required for certain decantings.
Connecticut NJSA can modify or terminate non-charitable trusts with all interested parties' consent without a material purpose violation. Charitable trusts require AG involvement.
CT SOS is central filing office for UCC liens. Fixture filings go to the town clerk in the town where real property is located. No separate local filing system for non-fixture collateral.
Connecticut imposes income tax on trusts with CT nexus. Connecticut has its own estate tax separate from federal, with a lower exemption threshold.
open_questions: Specific CT nexus tests for nonresident trusts require DRS guidance verification.

rule_summary: Connecticut homestead exemption for primary residence with income/age eligibility. Wage garnishment limited to 15% of gross weekly wages above minimum wage threshold.
open_questions: Exact dollar value caps for homestead exemption require DRS/Official compiler verification.
